chat.title: A table that feels like home
chat.lede: Rooms for every location, speech in character and out of it, dice that land in the conversation, and a Storyteller who answers in prose. This scene uses the real chat components; switch the language above to read it in Greek.
chat.note: Character names and game terms such as Hunger or Messy critical stay in English in every language.
chat.mara1: The Prince's herald is watching the door. I keep my smile thin and my hands where he can see them.
chat.mara2: “Good evening. I was told the gallery stays open late for friends of the Court.”
chat.ooc: can I roll Insight to read him? he seems nervous
chat.ai1: You read him at once: the herald is afraid, and not of you. His eyes keep drifting to the east stair, where the candles have burned down to stubs and no one has come to replace them. But the Beast reads him too. It smells the sweat under his collar, hears the quick bird-heartbeat in his throat, and for one long moment you are not sure which of you is smiling. He takes a step back. Somewhere above, a door closes very softly.
chat.action1: *steps back into the shadow of the colonnade and lets the herald breathe*
chat.jonah1: While he’s rattled, I slip past him toward the east stair.
chat.ai2: Your foot finds the one step that creaks. The herald turns, and the Hunger answers before you can think: your lips pull back from your teeth. Two Kindred in the gallery have seen it.

editions.v5r1: Every die showing 6 or more is a success; the Difficulty is how many you need.
editions.v5r2: Each pair of 10s adds two more: a critical.
editions.v5r3: Red Hunger dice can make a win messy or a failure bestial.
editions.c1: Roll your pool against a difficulty from 3 to 10.
editions.c2: Every 1 cancels a success. Four is exceptional, five or more phenomenal.
editions.c3: No successes and a 1 on the table: a botch.
editions.title: Roll the bones
editions.lede: Each chronicle picks its rules: the classic Revised dice or V5 with Hunger. Pick a pool and roll, or force an outcome to see every effect the table can show. The dice are resolved by the same code the game uses.

explain.success: Hits at or above the difficulty, minus one for every 1. One to three is a plain success.
explain.exceptional: Four net successes: an exceptional success.
explain.phenomenal: Five or more net successes: a phenomenal success.
explain.failure: The 1s cancelled every hit (or nothing hit). Nothing happens, for better or worse.
explain.botch: Not one die hit and a 1 showed: a botch. Something goes badly wrong.
explain.win: Successes (6 or more) meet the Difficulty.
explain.critical: A pair of 10s adds two more successes: a critical win.
explain.messy: A critical with a 10 on a Hunger die: you win, but the Beast decides how.
explain.fail: Some successes, but fewer than the Difficulty.
explain.bestial: A failure with a 1 on a Hunger die: the Beast lashes out.

glyphs.kicker: Drawn by hand, for this table
glyphs.title: A grimoire of {{count}} glyphs
glyphs.lede: No emoji and no borrowed icon font: every mark here is an original drawing on a 24px grid. Clan and discipline sigils are abstract designs of our own, not copies of official logos. Hover a glyph to watch it drawn again; pick one to inspect it.

atmo.fullHint: Fog drifts, candles flicker, dice tumble and blood drips.
atmo.subtleHint: Ambient loops hold still; short effects still play.
atmo.offHint: No motion at all. Every effect shows its final frame.
atmo.label: Atmosphere
atmo.system: Your device asks for reduced motion, so the atmosphere stays off.

hero.kicker: Theme preview · World of Darkness, classic and V5
hero.tagline: Gothic horror chronicles, told by a Storyteller that never sleeps.
hero.body: Classic and V5 dice, a table chat that feels like Discord, original horror glyphs and an AI Storyteller, in English and Greek. Everything below is the real interface, running live.

cta.title: The night is young.
cta.body: Your chronicle is waiting. Sign in with your account, or ask an admin for an invite code.

tokens.ratioHint: Ratios are computed live from the stylesheet. Surfaces show primary and muted text on them; every other colour is measured on the page background, then on a panel. 4.5 and up passes AA for body text, 7 and up AAA.
tokens.greekHint: Greek capitals drop their accents. The browser does this for us when the text is marked as Greek, so headings never show stray tonos marks.
tokens.title: Palette and type
tokens.lede: Night blues, bone whites and one red that means blood. Every text colour is checked against the surfaces it sits on, and every font covers Greek.
